assessment: Assignment changes and renames concentrate the observed difficulties, but do not establish why files are judged incomplete. Distinguish genuine omissions from identity confusion before selecting a bounded change. The sample establishes neither isolation for split courses nor the causes of handling time.

openings.claim: Using current instructor assignment to select a requested week's courses may make historical exports change after reassignment. Selecting through center-scoped course identity and assignment effective dates could prevent those omissions.
openings.delta: Treat a weekly export as a historical query whose course membership should remain stable across subsequent instructor changes.
openings.prediction: For fabricated attendance held fixed, reassigning an instructor changes the incumbent export's course set; effective-date selection restores the coordinator-confirmed set.
openings.probe: Replay one fabricated week before and after instructor reassignment, holding center, course identities and attendance constant. Compare expected course membership and CSV rows. If reproduced, estimate the smallest effective-date correction and verify unchanged schema, uninterrupted attendance entry and center isolation before committing the six-day budget.
assumptions: Course selection actually depends on instructor assignment.
Adequate assignment history exists or a bounded correction is feasible within six engineer-days and current hosting.

openings.claim: Are renamed courses present but unrecognized when coordinators compare exported names against older local timetables?
openings.delta: Test whether some replacement requests reflect identity confusion rather than absent attendance. A private old-name-to-current-name receipt could then reduce checking without changing the CSV.
openings.prediction: Affected rows remain present under the new name, and a rename receipt reduces false missing-course reports while preserving detection of a deliberately omitted course.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators' sessions for counterbalanced fabricated timetable/CSV comparisons with and without a rename receipt, including an omitted-course control. Record checking time, false alarms and missed omissions inside the private service or authorized workspace. Advance only if benefit and implementation effort justify the bounded change.
assumptions: Renames preserve a recoverable course identity.
A rename receipt is not evidence that course splits or cross-center isolation are correct.
